guide.whycantisleep.guide.category.sleep: Why the bed says no, and what to do about it.
- {#FFFFFF}Groggy{/}: Slowness, 1 min
- {#FFFFFF}Stiff Back{/}: Mining Fatigue, 1 min
- {#FFFFFF}Woke Up Starving{/}: Hunger, 30 s
- {#FFFF55}Pounding Headache{/}: Nausea, 10 s
- {#FFFF55}Weak Limbs{/}: Weakness, 1 min
- {#55FFFF}Bleary Eyes{/}: Blindness, 5 s (40 or less)
- {#FF55FF}Haunted{/}: Darkness and Bad Luck (30 or less)
- {#FFAA00}Cursed Dream{/}: Poison and Weakness (20 or less)

- {#FFFFFF}Sweet Dreams{/}: Regeneration, 30 s
- {#FFFFFF}Early Bird{/}: Speed, 1 min
- {#FFFFFF}Refreshed{/}: Haste, 1 min
- {#FFFF55}Clear Mind{/}: Night Vision, 2 min
- {#FFFF55}Dreamt of a Feast{/}: a full belly
- {#55FFFF}Dreamt of Victory{/}: Strength, 1 min (60+)
- {#55FFFF}Lucky Dream{/}: Luck, 5 min (70+)
- {#FF55FF}Heroic Dream{/}: Absorption and Resistance (80+)
- {#FFAA00}Dream of Flight{/}: Slow Falling, Jump Boost and Speed (90+)

After any night:

- {#FFFFFF}Vivid Dream{/}: Glowing, 30 s
- {#FFFFFF}Night Owl{/}: Night Vision, 45 s
- {#FFFF55}Dream of Fire{/}: Fire Resistance, 2 min
- {#FFFF55}Dream of the Sea{/}: Water Breathing and Dolphin's Grace
- {#55FFFF}Restless Legs{/}: Jump Boost, with Mining Fatigue

Waking in the morning, half the time you wake with a **sleep effect**: good after a good night, bad after a bad one, and now and then something odd.

Each has a rarity, which sets how often it comes and the color it is named in: {#FFFFFF}common{/}, {#FFFF55}uncommon{/}, {#55FFFF}rare{/}, {#FF55FF}epic{/}, {#FFAA00}legendary{/}. The rarer good ones need better nights, the rarer bad ones worse.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.h:
Run into a hiding spot with something on your heels and you must keep your heart slow while it is near.

Beats cross a pulse line from right to left. Press {key:key.attack} as each passes through the **green window** to steady it.

Clicking too early or too late, letting a beat pass, or making noise breaks one of your **three hearts**. At the third you gasp, and whatever chased you in hears it.

Hold {key:key.sneak} and use a hiding spot with **empty hands** to get in. Hidden, nothing can see you: whatever was after you loses you.

Stay hidden long enough (**15 seconds**, less with walls close round you) and what chased you in gives up and vanishes in smoke, along with the monsters prowling round the spot, even the ones that kept you from sleeping there.

> They only vanish if every other player nearby is hiding too. Someone out in the open, and they just lose you.

Press {key:key.sneak} again to come out. Being hurt brings you out too, and so does the spot breaking, another player opening it, or being found.

Out of a chest or a closet you stand right in front of it; out of anything else, where you went in.

Bosses aren't fooled: the Wither, the Ender Dragon, the Warden and Elder Guardians still see you.

Your eyes narrow to a squint that sways with your breath, tightens when monsters are near, and blinks now and then.

A card says what is out there. With monsters near, its timer counts down how long you must hold out.

You hear what prowls round you: muffled footsteps on whatever they walk on, and their shuffling when they stand.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.q:
Trying to walk or jump, or swinging the view about, makes **noise**. With monsters near, the card tells you to hold still.

Hold {key:key.whycantisleep.hold_breath} to hold your breath: no noise at all, for eight seconds, until you **gasp**, which is loud. It comes back slowly.

Make too much noise with a monster near the spot and you're **heard**: pulled out, with everything that chased you in coming for you at once.
Now and then a silverfish or a cave spider is already in the spot, and comes out at you instead.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.s:
What chased you in doesn't just wander off. After a moment it comes to your spot, stops in front of it and **looks about**, now and then right at you.

Then it either **finds you** and drags you out, or walks away.

The chance it finds you is **25%** on normal, half that on easy, half as much again on hard, and none on peaceful. Noise you make adds to it.
Another player who opens the chest or closet door you hide behind **finds you**, and you come out in front of them.
Crawl under any bed and lie flat on the floor. It needs a **floor** under it to lie on: a bed over air turns you away, and breaking the floor brings you out.
Two **top slabs** or **upside-down stairs** side by side, with **carpet** on both and a floor under both, make a table to hide under. Use the table or the carpet on it.

Climb into a **double chest**; a single one is too small. Its lid stays open a crack, and you peer out through the gap, turning only so far.

A double chest holds **two**, one in each half.
A door, or a double door, with a nook behind it **two blocks high**, shut in on every other side, roof and floor too, with room to stand. The door shuts behind you.

- The nook is one block wide for a door, two for a double door, which holds **two**.
- Walls can be blocks, or **trapdoors** lying flush against the nook: open ones for walls, shut ones for a roof.
- The door must open **out** of the nook: place it from inside, looking out.

> A spot with someone in it, or a monster, can't take another.

Three to build follow, to step through: one of planks, one walled with trapdoors, and a double closet for two.
One door for one; a double door, a nook behind each, for two.

- `#whycantisleep:blocks_sleep`, `does_not_block_sleep`: which mobs keep you up
- `#whycantisleep:ignores_hiding`: who sees through hiding
- `#whycantisleep:soothing`, `unsettling`: things by the bed
- `#whycantisleep:calm`, `creepy`, `loud`: jukebox songs

Under `data/<namespace>/whycantisleep/`:

- `sleep_modifier/`: what counts toward a night's score
- `sleep_effect/`: what you wake with
- `hiding_spot/`: any block as a hiding spot

The mod's own are files of the same kind, so a pack can change them, or turn one off with `"disabled": true`.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.packs.se:
Almost everything can be turned off or tuned in the server config, and it applies to everyone:

- highlights, arrows, room clearing, the Bedtime panel, nudges and the vote
- hiding, each kind of spot, the hide time, cover, critters, noise
- the heartbeat minigame, monsters searching and their chance, monsters vanishing
- sleep quality, night terrors, well rested, sleep effects and their chance

> Each player has their own settings for what they see.
Within six blocks of the bed (three up and down): **flowers** (potted ones too), **candles**, **amethyst**, **moss**, azaleas, spore blossoms, lily pads, **bookshelves** and cake. Each is worth +2, up to +10.

**Skulls and heads**, **cobwebs**, **sculk**, spawners, wither roses, bone blocks, soul lanterns, torches and campfires, creaking hearts, pale hanging moss and open eyeblossoms. Each is worth -3, down to -15.

> Their tooltips say which they are, and what they're worth.

- {#55FF55}+10{/} **Behind Closed Doors**: a closed room
- {#55FF55}+10{/} **Good Bedtime Routine**: a closed, lit room, slept till morning
- {#55FF55}+10{/} **Soothing Melody**: calm music, and nothing else playing
- {#55FF55}+2{/} each **Calming Things Nearby**, up to +10

- {#FF5555}-5{/} **Out in the Open**
- {#FF5555}-10{/} **Unlit Corners**: a closed room with dark spots
- {#FF5555}-5{/} **Light in Your Eyes**: a bright light at the pillow
- {#FF5555}-6{/} each **Prowling Monsters** within 24 blocks, up to -30
- {#FF5555}-20{/} **Eerie Music**, {#FF5555}-15{/} **Blaring Music**
- {#FF5555}-3{/} each **Creepy Things Nearby**, up to -15

- {#FF5555}-10{/} **Restless Mind**: you've been sleeping badly
- {#FF5555}-20{/} **Days Without Sleep**
- {#FF5555}-15{/} **Haunting Nightmare**: a night terror
- {#FF5555}-25{/} **Woke Before Dawn**: got up, hurt, or the bed broke

A jukebox playing within 16 blocks counts.

- {#55FF55}Calm{/}: cat, chirp, far, mall, stal, strad, wait, Creator (Music Box), Precipice, Tears
- {#FF5555}Creepy{/}: 11, 13, ward, 5, mellohi
- {#FF5555}Loud{/}: Pigstep, otherside, blocks, Creator, Lava Chicken

Each night is scored from **0 to 100**, starting at 75, from everything about it: the room, the light, monsters, music, things by the bed, and how you have been sleeping.

In the morning a card shows the score, a word for it and what mattered most:

- {#55FF55}Great{/} 85 and up, {#55FF55}Good{/} 65 and up
- {#FFFF55}Fair{/} 45 and up
- {#FF5555}Poor{/} 25 and up, {#FF5555}Awful{/} below

Sleep through to morning in a **closed room** that is **lit all through**, doors shut and no dark corners, and you wake well rested, with a little Regeneration.

A room is closed when the air round the bed, through open doors, stays small (under 600 blocks), close by, and never sees the sky.

Refused sleeps in a row and days without lying down add up:

- **Rested**: all is well.
- **Restless**: two refusals, or two days.
- **Sleepless**: five refusals, or three days, when phantoms come.

A **moon** in the corner of the screen fills up with each day without sleep, full at three.
Restless, lying down has a chance of a **night terror** (twice that sleepless): the dark goes red, a heartbeat quickens, eyes open in the dark... and you wake up **shaken**, with nausea and slowness.
The moon button on your player in the **inventory** shows how you have been sleeping and how your last night went: its score, what mattered most, and what you woke with.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.sleeping:
With another player online, lying in bed shows the **Bedtime** panel: how many are asleep as a bar, one segment for each sleeper the night needs, and who is still awake and why: awake, mining, fighting, away, or in another dimension.

**Click** an awake player to nudge them: a bell and a message, then a cooldown.

When only one player is still up, those in bed can **vote** from the panel to skip the night.

Once everyone in bed has voted, the players still up are asked in chat: *Go ahead* or *Not yet*. *Not yet* ends the vote for a minute; no answer in 30 seconds skips the night.
A bed within three blocks of another player who is asleep lets a couple of monsters by: sharing a room is braver than sleeping alone.

When monsters keep you from sleeping, exactly the ones that stopped you **glow** for a few seconds, colored by the kind of threat: creepers, endermen and raiders, the undead, and the rest each have their own color.

The most dangerous of them, a creeper above all and then the nearest, throbs brighter and gets a larger pointer.

> Only you see the glow. A server can show it to players without the mod too.

- **Arrows** around the crosshair point to the ones outside your view.
- A monster in view but **behind blocks** gets a ring where it is, pulsing out like a sound you'd hear.
- They leave **footprints** in their colors where they walked, for a while after the glow is gone.

The card above the hotbar says how many there are and where the closest is: *3 monsters nearby, closest: Zombie, 6 blocks below*.

A bed that says no always says why, and what to do:

- **Monsters nearby**: deal with them, or hide.
- **Not the time**: beds work at night and in thunderstorms.
- **Too far**: stand next to the bed.
- **Obstructed**: something is in the way above it.
- **Occupied**: someone is already in it.
- **Other players awake**: how many more must sleep.

In the Nether and the End beds explode. The first try only {#FF5555}warns{/}; use it again within three seconds to go through with it.

Deal with every monster that blocked your sleep within **10 seconds**, with nothing else coming near, and the room is safe.

Still standing by the bed, you lie straight down in it.

> The monsters still count until they are gone, so a dying one keeps you up a moment longer.
